question: How much slack does the three-second readiness bound actually have?
method: The test helper was temporarily instrumented to report the time from the readiness wait until both feeds are ready, measured on a frozen debug build of the same test, then reverted. No bound was changed.

stochastic_reproduction.load: 12 competing spinners and two fsync loops on 16 cores
pinned to two cores with three spinners and two fsync loops
stochastic_reproduction.note: Stopped in favour of measuring the readiness margin directly.

interpretation: Competing load on two pinned cores with continuous fsync pressure only doubles the readiness time, from 11 to 23 ms.
For the bound to expire from host slowness alone, the runner would have to be about 108 times slower than that deliberately overloaded configuration.
The same failing job was not broadly slow: its kernel suite finished in 57.26 s against 59.45 s for the passing job, with individual tests matching within tenths of a second.
A discarded discovery error instead produces an unbounded wait, since the only feed then sleeps for an hour, which matches a clean three-second timeout on an otherwise healthy runner.
This is strong circumstantial evidence, not proof: the feed states at the time of the failure were never recorded. The helper now reports them, so a recurrence settles it.
